question.problem:
Consider the function

$$
f(x)=1[x\ge -1]\cdot {x}^{2}+1[x<-1]\cdot (-x).
$$

What is $f(-3)?$
question.worked_solution:
The indicator function $1[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false.

$$
1[P]=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }P\text{ is true}, \\ 0, & \text{if }P\text{ is false}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=-3,$ we evaluate each indicator function:

- $1[x\ge -1]=1[-3\ge -1]=0$ (since $-3\ge -1$ is false)

- $1[x<-1]=1[-3<-1]=1$ (since $-3<-1$ is true)

Substituting into the expression for $f(x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) & =1[-3\ge -1]\cdot (-3)^{2}+1[-3<-1]\cdot (-(-3)) \\  & =0\cdot 9+1\cdot 3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the indicator functions act as a "switch": since $x=-3<-1,$ the first term vanishes and only the second term contributes to the result.
